Fundamentals of Amazon EC2

Learn the AWS compute models and Amazon EC2: AMIs, instance types, connection methods, the lifecycle, security, and pricing models.

Overview and Objectives

Lesson Overview

In this lesson, you learn the core concepts of AWS cloud computing, identify the primary components and features of Amazon EC2, compare EC2 instance types and pricing models, and select the appropriate instance configuration for real-world workloads.

Mastering Amazon EC2 and the AWS compute models is essential for the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) exam and the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) exam. Compute architectures and instance configurations make up a large part of the scenario-based questions. The exams test your ability to match a workload to the correct instance family, to decode instance names, to choose a pricing model, and to secure and connect to instances.

This lesson supports the Module 267 scenario, in which you help RetailCloud. The last tab checks what you learned.

The tabs in this lesson cover the following topics:

  • Tab 1: AWS compute models, what Amazon EC2 is, its key characteristics and features, and Amazon Machine Images (AMIs).
  • Tab 2: EC2 instance types, the naming convention, the StreamPulse case study, and the basic configuration options for an instance.
  • Tab 3: the ways to connect to an instance, the classic ports to know, the instance lifecycle, and the first hands-on lab.
  • Tab 4: security groups, IAM roles, NAT devices, key pairs, and overall EC2 security.
  • Tab 5: the OSRSD pricing models, Spot Instances and the second hands-on lab, Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances, and a quick comparison.
  • Tab 6: open-ended Knowledge Check questions with model answers.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:

  1. Identify the core features and components of Amazon EC2, including AMIs, security groups, key pairs, and EBS volumes.
  2. Explain the EC2 instance naming syntax and summarize the functional differences between EC2 instance families: General Purpose, Compute, Memory, Storage, and Accelerated.
  3. Select appropriate connection methods.
  4. Compare the OSRSD pricing models (On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot Instances, and Dedicated Hosts) to align workload constraints with optimal financial models.
  5. Assess cloud architecture scenarios to diagnose performance bottlenecks and determine cost-effective EC2 configurations for diverse workloads.
  6. Launch and securely access an EC2 instance.

1. Compute on AWS and Amazon EC2

Problem Statement

RetailCloud’s operations team has a legacy accounting application that needs Windows Server and custom software, and the web team needs ten identical web servers for a sale. Both teams ask the architect which AWS compute option to use, what an EC2 instance is made of, and how to launch identical servers quickly.

The architect must explain the AWS compute models, name the components of an EC2 instance, and show how an AMI makes servers repeatable.

Your challenge:

  • Name the AWS compute models and say where Amazon EC2 fits.
  • List the components of an EC2 instance.
  • Explain what an AMI contains and how to use it in another Region.

1.1 What Is Computing on the AWS Platform?

Computing on AWS refers to cloud-based services that process data with high-performance processors capable of serving many virtual instances at the same time. AWS compute resources remove the need for physical hardware investments, so organizations can deploy and scale applications dynamically in the cloud.

1.1.1 Categories of AWS Compute

AWS provides several compute models:

  • Virtual machines (for example, AWS EC2): infrastructure as a service (IaaS).
  • Containers (for example, Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS): container orchestration.
  • Serverless containers (for example, AWS Fargate): serverless infrastructure for containers.
  • Serverless code (for example, AWS Lambda): function as a service (FaaS).
  • Managed application platforms.
  • Batch and high-performance computing.

AWS organizes its major compute options around instances, containers, and serverless computing. For more information, see the AWS compute overview. Lessons 273.1 and 273.5 cover AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, and AWS Fargate.

1.2 What Is Amazon EC2?

Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) is a web service that provides resizable compute capacity in the form of virtual servers in the cloud. It is one of the cornerstone components of the AWS cloud platform. The virtual servers are called instances.

The following diagram shows the key components of an EC2 instance:

  • An image: a template that contains the software to run on your instance, such as the operating system.
  • A key pair: a set of security credentials that you use to prove your identity when you connect to your instance. The public key is on your instance, and the private key is on your computer.
  • A network: a virtual private cloud (VPC) is a virtual network dedicated to your AWS account. To help you get started quickly, your account has a default VPC in each AWS Region, and each default VPC has a default subnet in each Availability Zone.
  • A security group: acts as a virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic.
  • An EBS volume: a root volume is required for the image. You can optionally add data volumes.

1.3 Key Characteristics of Amazon EC2

  • Virtual instances: an instance is a virtual server that runs on AWS infrastructure. Each instance works like an isolated virtual machine with its own virtual CPU, memory, storage, operating system, and network interface. Many instances can run at the same time on one physical host.
  • Elasticity and scalability: you can scale compute capacity up or down quickly, without buying hardware, to follow changing workload demand.
  • Cost efficiency: EC2 uses a pay-as-you-go model, so you pay only for the compute resources that you use instead of investing capital in hardware planned years in advance.
  • Reduced management overhead: AWS manages the physical hardware, the data centers, and the virtualization layer, so you do not maintain physical servers. Under the shared responsibility model, you still manage the guest operating system, security patches, installed software, and security group rules (section 4.6).

1.3.1 Example Scenario

A company is migrating a legacy accounting application that requires Windows Server and custom software installation. Amazon EC2 is appropriate because the company needs control over the operating system and the application environment.

1.4 Features of Amazon EC2

  • Instances: virtual servers.
  • Amazon Machine Images (AMIs): preconfigured templates for your instances that package the components you need for your server, including the operating system and additional software.
  • Instance types: various configurations of CPU, memory, storage, networking capacity, and graphics hardware for your instances.
  • Amazon EBS volumes: persistent storage volumes for your data, using Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
  • Instance store volumes: storage volumes for temporary data. The data is deleted when you stop, hibernate, or terminate your instance.
  • Key pairs: secure login information for your instances. AWS stores the public key, and you store the private key in a secure place.
  • Security groups: a virtual firewall that lets you specify the protocols, ports, and source IP ranges that can reach your instances, and the destination IP ranges to which your instances can connect.

1.5 Amazon Machine Images (AMIs)

An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is a template that contains the information needed to launch an EC2 instance. You choose an AMI when you launch an instance, because it decides the operating system and the software that the instance starts with. One AMI can launch many instances, and every one of them starts with the same configuration.

1.5.1 What an AMI Contains

  • A template for the root volume: usually an operating system, and often an application server and applications.
  • Launch permissions: they control which AWS accounts can use the AMI to launch instances. A new AMI is private to your account until you share it.
  • A block device mapping: it lists the volumes to attach to the instance when it launches, such as the root volume and any data volumes.

1.5.2 Where AMIs Come From

  • AWS-provided AMIs: images that AWS maintains for common operating systems, such as Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, and Windows Server.
  • AWS Marketplace AMIs: images from software vendors that include preinstalled software. Some carry an extra software charge.
  • Community AMIs: images that other AWS users share. AWS cannot guarantee their integrity or security, so review an AMI before you use it.
  • Your own AMIs: images that you create from an instance that you configured.

1.5.3 Creating and Using an AMI

You can turn one configured instance into a reusable template:

  1. Launch an instance from an existing AMI.
  2. Install and configure your software, and apply the latest patches.
  3. Create an AMI from the instance. For an EBS-backed AMI, EC2 saves snapshots of the instance’s volumes.
  4. Launch new instances from your AMI. Each new instance starts with the same configuration.

1.5.4 AMIs and Regions

  • An AMI belongs to one Region. To launch an instance in another Region, copy the AMI to that Region with the EC2 console, the AWS CLI, or the CopyImage API action. The copy has a new AMI ID.

1.5.5 Important Points

  • An AMI is not an instance. It captures the volumes at the time that you create it, so later changes to the source instance are not in the AMI.
  • The AMI itself has no charge, but the EBS snapshots behind it incur storage charges. Deregistering an AMI does not delete its snapshots, so delete them separately when you no longer need them.
  • Do not share an AMI that contains secrets, such as private keys or passwords.

1.5.6 Example Scenario

A company configures one web server with the operating system, the web server software, and the latest patches. It creates an AMI from that server and launches ten identical servers from the AMI. When the company expands to a second Region, it copies the AMI to that Region first.

Exam tip: When an SAA-C03 question asks how to launch many identical servers quickly, or how to recreate a configured server in another Region, the answer is a custom AMI, copied to the target Region.

1.6 Exam-Style Questions

This question is new for this lesson.

1.6.1 Exam-Style Question

Written for this course.

Scenario: A company configures one web server with its software and patches. It must launch ten identical servers in us-east-1 now, and it must recreate the same servers in eu-west-1 next month. What should the company do? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. Create an AMI from the configured server, launch the servers from it, and copy the AMI to eu-west-1 when needed.
  • B. Create a snapshot of the instance store volume, and launch the servers from the snapshot in eu-west-1.
  • C. Stop the configured server, move it to eu-west-1, and start it again.
  • D. Share the key pair with the new servers so that they have the same configuration.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: A. An AMI is the template that makes identical instances repeatable, and an AMI belongs to one Region, so the company copies it to the second Region.

OptionResultReason
ACorrectA custom AMI launches many identical servers, and copying it to another Region lets the company launch there.
BIncorrectInstance store data is temporary and is not saved in snapshots, and a snapshot alone is not a launch template.
CIncorrectAn instance cannot be moved to another Region. You copy an AMI and launch a new instance.
DIncorrectA key pair holds login credentials. It does not carry software or configuration.

2. Instance Types and Configuration

Problem Statement

RetailCloud runs very different workloads: a login API, a video-encoding job, an in-memory cache, a machine learning recommender, and development servers. One size of instance for all of them wastes money, and the wrong family causes slow jobs and dropped requests.

The architect needs to read instance names and match each workload to the right instance family.

Your challenge:

  • Name the instance families and the workloads that fit them.
  • Decode an instance type such as c7gn.xlarge.
  • List the basic options that you choose when you launch an instance.

2.1 EC2 Instance Types

  • AWS allocates hardware resources to your instances according to the instance type that you select.
  • AWS offers hundreds of instance types, organized into six groups: general purpose, compute optimized, memory optimized, storage optimized, accelerated computing, and high-performance computing (HPC) optimized. For the complete list, see Amazon EC2 instance types.
  • Newer generations are added over time, and older generations become previous-generation types.

2.1.1 Can You Change the EC2 Instance Type?

Yes. Stop the instance, modify its instance type, and then start it again. The new instance type must be compatible with your AMI and within the limits of the selected Availability Zone. Resizing is a common practice when you right-size workloads or optimize performance and cost.

2.2 Amazon EC2 Instance Type Naming Conventions

Amazon EC2 provides a variety of instance types so that you can choose the type that best meets your requirements. The name follows this format:

c7gn.xlarge = instance family + generation + processor and capabilities + size

  • Instance family: the series letter, such as C for compute optimized, M for general purpose, R for memory optimized, or T for burstable performance.
  • Generation: AWS improves the families over time, and the number shows the generation.
  • Processor and capabilities: one or more lowercase letters after the generation. For example, g means AWS Graviton processors, a means AMD processors, i means Intel processors, d means instance store volumes, n means network and EBS optimized, e means extra storage or memory, and z means high CPU frequency. Not every instance type has these letters.
  • Size: the size within the instance family, for example micro, small, medium, large, and xlarge.
  • Example: c7gn.xlarge is a compute optimized instance (c) of the seventh generation (7), with AWS Graviton processors (g) and network and EBS optimization (n), in the xlarge size.
FamilyGroupUse caseExample workloads
CCompute optimizedCPU-intensiveBatch processing, gaming
RMemory optimized (RAM)Memory-intensiveDatabases, caching
MGeneral purposeBalanced compute, memory, and networkWeb servers, applications
TGeneral purpose, burstableVariable workloads that burstDevelopment and test, low traffic
P and GAccelerated computing (GPU)Graphics and machine learningMachine learning, rendering
I, D, and HStorage optimizedStorage-intensive, high I/ODatabases, data warehousing

The course uses the mnemonic CRAM-FACTS-PIG to recall the family letters.

Tip: start with the latest generation that fits your workload. Newer generations usually give better price performance than older ones, but check the specifications of the type that you choose. For more detail, see Amazon EC2 instance type naming conventions.

2.3 Real-World Scenario: Re-Architecting a Media Streaming and Analytics Platform

Company: StreamPulse Inc., a fictional company used as an example.

Application: a high-throughput video streaming platform that ingests user uploads, encodes video files, serves live streams, processes real-time viewing metrics, and runs deep learning recommendations.

2.3.1 The Challenge

During a quarterly architecture review, the Cloud Engineering team noticed two major issues:

  1. Severe performance bottlenecks: video encoding jobs were taking hours, and real-time viewing metrics were dropping packets during peak hours.
  2. Skyrocketing AWS bills: development servers and static microservices were running on expensive, over-provisioned instances 24 hours a day.

2.3.2 The Architectural Solution: Matching EC2 Families to Workloads

The Lead Architect maps each component of the platform to the instance family that fits its resource demands:

ComponentFamily and exampleWhy it fitsOutcome
Application core and authentication APIGeneral purpose (m6i.xlarge)The workload manages login sessions, API routing, and business logic. It needs a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4 GB of RAM per vCPU).Stable API response times with predictable performance.
Video encoding and transcoding engineCompute optimized (c6i.4xlarge)It converts raw 4K video into several resolutions with CPU-bound algorithms. The C family offers a high CPU-to-memory ratio (1:2) and high-clock-speed processors.Video rendering time decreased by 65 percent.
Real-time viewer analytics cacheMemory optimized (r6g.2xlarge)It runs an in-memory Redis database for millions of active viewer streams. The R family delivers a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (8 GB per vCPU), and in-memory data sets stay in RAM for microsecond reads and writes.Database timeouts ended during peak live events, and cache hit rates rose to 98 percent.
Machine learning video recommendationsAccelerated computing (g4dn.xlarge)It runs deep learning models on video metadata and user history. The G family includes NVIDIA GPUs for parallel processing such as machine learning inference.Real-time recommendation latency dropped under 50 ms.
Internal development, test, and staging environmentsBurstable general purpose (t4g.small)The microservices run during business hours with low traffic. The T family uses a baseline CPU credit model, stays low-cost when idle, and can burst up to 100 percent CPU during integration tests.Staging infrastructure costs fell by 70 percent.

The outcome numbers belong to the fictional example.

When you launch an instance, you choose these options:

What you chooseEC2 term

2.5 Exam-Style Question

This question comes from the course lesson document.

2.5.1 Exam-Style Question

From the course lesson document.

Scenario: A company is migrating an internal financial analytics system to AWS. It has three components. First, an in-memory data grid (Redis) holds millions of account balances for microsecond-level query speeds. Second, a batch job processing engine performs heavy mathematical calculations and media rendering every night. Third, a low-traffic development and staging web portal is used intermittently by developers during business hours. The solutions architect must select the most cost-effective and performant EC2 instance family for each component. Which combination should the architect select? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. Component 1: C-series; Component 2: R-series; Component 3: M-series.
  • B. Component 1: R-series; Component 2: C-series; Component 3: T-series.
  • C. Component 1: M-series; Component 2: C-series; Component 3: R-series.
  • D. Component 1: R-series; Component 2: T-series; Component 3: C-series.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: B. The in-memory grid needs memory (R), the batch engine is CPU-bound (C), and the intermittent portal fits a burstable instance (T).

OptionResultReason
AIncorrectThis swaps the R-series and C-series roles. It puts compute-optimized instances on an in-memory cache and memory-optimized instances on a batch engine.
BCorrectR-series gives the most memory for the Redis grid, C-series gives high CPU for the nightly calculations, and T-series is a low-cost burstable choice for an intermittent portal.
CIncorrectM-series (general purpose) for an in-memory database is under-provisioned on RAM and unnecessarily expensive for general compute capacity.
DIncorrectT-series on a heavy batch engine would quickly exhaust its CPU credits and cause extreme processing lag.

3. Connecting, Ports, and Lifecycle

Problem Statement

RetailCloud’s administrators need to log in to Linux and Windows instances without opening the instances to the whole internet. They also need to know in which instance states AWS stops billing for compute.

The architect must choose connection methods, recognize the classic ports, and read the instance lifecycle.

Your challenge:

  • Select a connection method for a Linux instance, a Windows instance, and an instance with no public IP address.
  • Name the ports for SSH, RDP, and HTTPS.
  • Say which instance states are billed.

3.1 Ways to Connect to an Amazon EC2 Instance

#Connection methodOperating systemDescription
1SSH clientLinuxConnect with an SSH client such as OpenSSH, Terminal, PowerShell, or PuTTY. The instance must be reachable over the network, and its security group normally allows inbound TCP port 22 from an approved IP address.
2Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) clientWindowsConnect with Microsoft Remote Desktop or another RDP client. The instance must be reachable, and its security group normally allows inbound TCP port 3389 from an approved IP address.
3EC2 Instance ConnectLinuxConnect through the EC2 console, the AWS CLI, or an SSH client. EC2 Instance Connect sends a temporary SSH public key to the instance. The instance must have EC2 Instance Connect installed and allow SSH traffic on port 22.
4AWS Systems Manager Session ManagerLinux and WindowsStart a secure command-line session from the AWS console or the AWS CLI. The instance does not need a public IP address or an inbound SSH or RDP rule. The instance must be managed by Systems Manager and have the required IAM permissions and SSM Agent.
5EC2 Instance Connect EndpointLinux and WindowsCreates a secure tunnel to an instance through its private IP address. The instance does not need a public IP address, an internet gateway, a VPN, or a bastion host. It supports SSH for Linux and RDP for Windows. Appropriate IAM permissions and security group rules are required.
6Systems Manager Fleet Manager Remote DesktopWindowsProvides browser-based Remote Desktop access to a Windows instance. It uses Systems Manager, so you can manage the instance without exposing RDP port 3389 directly to the internet.
7AWS CloudShellPrimarily Linux, through SSH or the AWS CLICloudShell provides a browser-based, preauthenticated command-line environment. You can use it to run AWS CLI commands or start an SSH connection, but CloudShell is not itself an EC2 remote-access service. The EC2 instance must still be reachable through an appropriate network path.

3.2 Classic Ports to Know for EC2

PortProtocolUse
22SSH (Secure Shell)Log in to a Linux instance.
21FTP (File Transfer Protocol)Upload files to a file share.
22SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol)Upload files by using SSH.
80HTTPAccess unsecured websites.
443HTTPSAccess secured websites.
3389RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol)Log in to a Windows instance.

3.3 EC2 Instance Lifecycle

The table shows the instance states that a virtual machine can be in at a given time, and the billing for each.

Instance stateDescriptionBilling
pendingThe instance is preparing to enter the running state. An instance enters the pending state when it launches for the first time, or when it is started after being in the stopped state.Not billed
runningThe instance is running and ready for use.Billed
stoppingThe instance is preparing to be stopped or stop-hibernated.Not billed if preparing to stop. Billed if preparing to hibernate.
stoppedThe instance is shut down and cannot be used. The instance can be started at any time.Not billed
shutting-downThe instance is preparing to be terminated.Not billed
terminatedThe instance has been permanently deleted and cannot be started.Not billed

Note: Reserved Instances that are terminated are billed until the end of their term.

Scenario: A security team wants administrators to open command-line sessions to EC2 instances that have no public IP address and no inbound SSH rule. Which connection method fits? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. An SSH client over the internet.

3.5.2 Exam-Style Question

Written for this course.

Scenario: In which situation does AWS bill for compute while an instance is in the stopping state? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. The instance is preparing to stop.
  • B. The instance is preparing to hibernate.
  • C. The instance is preparing to be terminated.
  • D. The instance is in the pending state.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: B. An instance that is preparing to hibernate is billed while it is in the stopping state. An instance that is preparing to stop is not billed.

OptionResultReason
AIncorrectAn instance that is preparing to stop is not billed.
BCorrectAn instance that is preparing to hibernate is billed in the stopping state.
CIncorrectPreparing to be terminated is the shutting-down state, which is not billed.
DIncorrectThe pending state is not billed, and it is not the stopping state.

4. Securing EC2 Instances

Problem Statement

RetailCloud’s web servers must accept customer traffic, but the security team does not want the servers open to the world. Some servers are private and still need to download patches, and every login must use secure credentials.

The architect must explain the four tools that secure EC2 instances and say what the customer is responsible for.

Your challenge:

  • Describe how security groups control traffic.
  • Explain when an instance role or a NAT device is the right tool.
  • Describe how key pairs protect logins.

4.1 Securing EC2 Instances

AWS provides four tools to help you secure your EC2 instances: security groups, Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles, network address translation (NAT) instances, and key pairs.

4.2 Security Groups: The Firewall for an EC2 Instance

  • An EC2 security group acts as a virtual firewall that controls traffic to and from an EC2 instance’s network interface.
  • Security groups contain only allow rules. They do not support explicit deny or block rules.
  • A new security group has no inbound rules, so no inbound traffic is allowed. It has one outbound rule that allows all outbound traffic. You can modify or remove that default outbound rule.
  • Inbound rules control traffic that enters the associated resource, and outbound rules control traffic that leaves it.
  • Each rule can specify a protocol, such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP, a port or port range, a source for inbound traffic, or a destination for outbound traffic.
  • Security groups can authorize IPv4 and IPv6 traffic, but IPv4 and IPv6 need separate rules.
  • A security group can be associated with multiple EC2 instances, and an instance can have multiple security groups associated with its network interface.
  • Security groups are stateful. When traffic is allowed in one direction, the response traffic is automatically allowed, regardless of the rules in the opposite direction.
  • Security group rules have no numbered priorities and are not processed in a particular order. AWS evaluates all applicable rules before it decides whether to allow traffic.
  • You can add, modify, or remove rules at any time. Changes apply automatically to the associated network interfaces.
  • Security groups can reference IP address ranges, prefix lists, and other security groups.
  • To explicitly block a particular IP address or traffic pattern at the subnet level, use a network access control list, because security groups have no deny rules.

4.2.1 Example

A web server’s security group could allow HTTPS traffic on TCP port 443 from the internet, SSH traffic on TCP port 22 only from an administrator’s IP address, and all outbound traffic. Any inbound traffic that does not match an allow rule is denied.

4.3 Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles

  • You define an IAM role by giving it permissions to perform actions on specified services or resources in your AWS account.
  • When you assign a role to a resource, such as an EC2 instance, or to a user, they gain access to the resources that the role’s policies include.
  • You can assign an IAM role to an EC2 instance so that processes on the instance can reach the tools that they need, such as an Amazon RDS database instance, without stored credentials. Lesson 267.5 covers IAM in depth.

4.4 Network Address Translation (NAT) Devices

  • Sometimes you configure an EC2 instance without a public IP address to limit its exposure to the network. That also stops the instance from reaching the internet, which it needs, for example, to download security patches.
  • One solution is network address translation (NAT). It gives your private instance access to the internet without allowing access to the instance from the internet.
  • AWS provides a NAT instance or a NAT gateway. Both do the same job, but a NAT gateway is a managed service. Lesson 269.2 covers both.

4.5 Key Pairs

  • When you launch a new EC2 Linux instance, you are prompted to use an existing SSH key pair or to create a new one.
  • You get only one opportunity to download the private half of the key pair to your own computer. Store the private key file without exposing it publicly.
  • You can open a shell on a remote EC2 instance with: ssh -i keyname.pem ec2-user@<public_ip_address_of_instance>.

4.6 Overall EC2 Security

  • When you deploy an Amazon EC2 instance, you are responsible for managing the guest operating system (including updates and security patches), any application software or utilities that you install on the instance, and the configuration of the AWS-provided firewall, the security group, on each instance.
  • Termination protection is disabled by default. Without it, you have no safeguard against accidentally terminating an instance. You must turn it on if you want that extra protection.
  • Amazon EC2 uses public-key cryptography to encrypt and decrypt login information. A public key encrypts a piece of data, such as a password, and the recipient uses the private key to decrypt it. The public and private keys are known as a key pair.
  • You can encrypt your root device volume, which holds the underlying operating system, when you create the instance or with third-party tools such as BitLocker. You can also encrypt additional EBS volumes.
  • By default, when you terminate an instance with an attached EBS root volume, the instance and the root volume are deleted together. Any additional EBS volume that is attached to the same instance is preserved. You can change this rule, but it is usually easier to start a new instance with a fresh root volume than to reuse an old one.

4.7 Exam-Style Questions

These two questions are new for this lesson.

4.7.1 Exam-Style Question

Written for this course.

Scenario: A security group allows inbound HTTPS traffic on port 443 from the internet. A solutions architect must block traffic from one specific IP address that is probing the web server. What should the architect do? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. Add a deny rule for that IP address to the security group.
  • B. Add an inbound rule that denies port 443 from that IP address.
  • C. Use a network access control list to deny that IP address at the subnet level.
  • D. Remove the default outbound rule from the security group.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: C. Security groups have only allow rules, so a deny must come from a network access control list at the subnet level.

OptionResultReason
AIncorrectSecurity groups do not support deny rules.
BIncorrectA security group cannot deny traffic. It can only allow traffic.
CCorrectA network access control list supports explicit deny rules at the subnet level.
DIncorrectOutbound rules do not control which sources can send inbound traffic.

4.7.2 Exam-Style Question

Written for this course.

Scenario: An EC2 instance in a private subnet has no public IP address. It must download security patches from the internet, and no one on the internet may be able to connect to it. Which solution fits? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. Assign a public IP address and allow all inbound traffic.
  • B. Use a NAT gateway so that the instance can start outbound connections to the internet.
  • C. Attach an additional EBS volume to the instance.
  • D. Create a new key pair for the instance.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: B. A NAT gateway gives a private instance outbound access to the internet without allowing inbound access from the internet.

OptionResultReason
AIncorrectA public IP address with open inbound traffic exposes the instance to the internet.
BCorrectA NAT gateway lets the private instance start outbound connections for patches while it stays unreachable from the internet.
CIncorrectAn EBS volume adds storage. It does not provide internet access.
DIncorrectA key pair protects logins. It does not provide internet access.

5. EC2 Pricing Models

Problem Statement

RetailCloud’s cloud bill keeps rising. Its production servers run all year, its sale-season capacity is unpredictable, and its nightly video jobs can restart if they stop. The finance team wants to pay the right price for each kind of workload.

The architect must compare the five EC2 pricing models and match each workload to one of them.

Your challenge:

  • Name the five OSRSD pricing models.
  • Match a workload to a model by its commitment and interruption tolerance.
  • Launch a Spot Instance in the lab.

5.1 EC2 Pricing Models (OSRSD)

Amazon EC2 offers five primary pricing models, which the course summarizes with the acronym OSRSD. They let you balance cost, flexibility, and availability based on your workload needs: On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot Instances, and Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances.

5.2 O: On-Demand Instances

On-Demand Instances let you pay for EC2 compute capacity as you use it, with no long-term commitment. This option gives the greatest flexibility, but it usually costs more than the commitment-based models.

Best for:

  • Short-term workloads.
  • Unpredictable demand.
  • Development and testing.
  • New applications with unknown usage patterns.

Example: a company launches temporary EC2 instances to test a new application for two weeks.

5.3 S: Savings Plans

Savings Plans give discounted compute pricing when you commit to a consistent amount of compute usage, measured in dollars per hour, for one or three years.

  • You pay for the committed hourly amount even when your actual usage is lower. For example, if you commit to $10 per hour but use only $7 per hour, you still pay the $10 hourly commitment.
  • Any eligible usage above the commitment is charged at the applicable regular rate.

The major types are:

  • Compute Savings Plans: provide greater flexibility across eligible compute services, instance families, sizes, operating systems, and Regions.
  • EC2 Instance Savings Plans: provide larger discounts but require a commitment to an EC2 instance family in a selected Region.

Best for: predictable compute spending, long-running applications, and organizations that want flexibility while they reduce cost.

Example: a company expects to spend at least $10 per hour on compute resources for the next three years, and it buys a Savings Plan to reduce costs.

5.4 R: Reserved Instances (RI)

  • Reserved Instances provide a billing discount in exchange for a one-year or three-year commitment. You pay for the reserved commitment even when you do not fully use it.
  • A Reserved Instance is primarily a billing discount, not an EC2 instance. If no running instance matches the reservation, you may still pay for the unused commitment.
  • They suit EC2 workloads with predictable and stable usage.

Important characteristics:

  • They are a pricing benefit, not a separate type of EC2 instance.
  • Standard Reserved Instances provide larger discounts but less flexibility.
  • Convertible Reserved Instances allow certain configuration changes but usually give a smaller discount.
  • Zonal Reserved Instances can provide a capacity reservation in a particular Availability Zone.

Best for: databases, enterprise applications, production servers that run continuously, and workloads with stable instance requirements.

Example: a company runs the same EC2-based payroll application continuously and buys Reserved Instances to reduce its long-term compute cost.

5.5 S: Spot Instances

An EC2 Spot Instance lets you use unused Amazon EC2 capacity at a large discount compared with On-Demand pricing. The tradeoff is that AWS can interrupt the instance when it needs the capacity back or when the Spot capacity is no longer available. AWS generally provides a two-minute interruption notice before it stops, hibernates, or terminates the instance.

Spot Instances are usage-based. You generally pay while the instance is running, but AWS may interrupt it. This differs from Reserved Instances, which involve a one-year or three-year pricing commitment.

5.5.1 Important Characteristics

  • Uses spare EC2 capacity.
  • Usually costs less than On-Demand instances.
  • Can be interrupted by AWS, and is not guaranteed to remain available.
  • Works best with flexible and fault-tolerant applications.
  • Can be launched individually or through an Auto Scaling group.
  • Pricing and availability vary by instance type, Availability Zone, and Region.

5.5.2 Real-World Scenario

A media company must process thousands of video files. Each file can be processed independently, and interrupted jobs can restart from a saved checkpoint. The company uses Spot Instances to process the videos at a lower cost. If AWS interrupts one of the instances, the unfinished job returns to a queue, and another instance processes it later. Spot Instances suit this workload because it can tolerate interruptions, can be restarted, does not need one specific instance to stay available, and benefits from lower compute cost.

5.5.3 Appropriate Use Cases

Spot Instances are commonly used for:

  • Batch processing.
  • Data analysis.
  • Video rendering and image processing.
  • Scientific computing.
  • Containerized workloads.
  • Stateless web application capacity.
  • Machine learning training.

5.5.4 When Not to Use Spot Instances

Avoid using Spot Instances as the only capacity for:

  • Critical databases.
  • Applications that cannot tolerate interruption.
  • Long-running jobs that cannot save progress.
  • Workloads that need guaranteed capacity.
  • A single production server with no redundancy.

Exam tip: When an SAA-C03 question describes a workload that is fault tolerant, flexible, stateless, interruptible, or able to retry, Spot Instances are often the most cost-effective answer. Remember that you generally pay for a Spot Instance only while it is running.

5.7 D: Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances (EC2 Tenancy)

  • These options run on hardware that is dedicated to a single AWS customer.
  • Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware, but AWS manages instance placement. They may share hardware with other instances in the same account, and you have no control over placement. An instance can move to different hardware after a stop and start.
  • Dedicated Hosts give you access to an entire physical server and greater visibility and control over how instances are placed.

Best for: regulatory or compliance requirements, strict physical-isolation requirements, server-bound software licenses, and Bring Your Own License scenarios.

Example: a company uses Dedicated Hosts because its commercial software licenses are tied to physical processor sockets.

5.8 Quick Comparison

Pricing modelCommitmentPotential interruptionBest use
On-DemandNoneNoShort-term or unpredictable workloads
Savings Plans1 or 3 yearsNoPredictable compute spending
Reserved Instances1 or 3 yearsNoStable EC2 configurations
Spot InstancesNoneYesFlexible, fault-tolerant workloads
Dedicated optionsVariesNoCompliance, isolation, or licensing

5.9 Exam-Style Questions

These two questions are new for this lesson.

5.9.1 Exam-Style Question

Written for this course.

Scenario: A company runs a nightly batch job that processes thousands of independent video files. Each job saves a checkpoint, and an interrupted job can restart on another instance. The company wants the lowest compute cost. Which purchasing option should it use? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. On-Demand Instances.
  • B. Spot Instances.
  • C. Dedicated Hosts.
  • D. A three-year Reserved Instance for a single instance.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: B. The workload is flexible and fault tolerant, which is the ideal fit for Spot Instances at a large discount.

OptionResultReason
AIncorrectOn-Demand is flexible but usually costs more than Spot for a workload that tolerates interruption.
BCorrectSpot Instances use unused capacity at a large discount, and this workload can restart after an interruption.
CIncorrectDedicated Hosts are for isolation or license needs, and they raise cost.
DIncorrectA three-year commitment for one instance does not match a flexible nightly batch workload.

5.9.2 Exam-Style Question

Written for this course.

Scenario: A company runs a payroll application on the same EC2 instance type every day for the next three years. The company can commit to this usage. Which option lowers the cost while it keeps the instance always available? Which solution meets the requirements?

  • A. Spot Instances.
  • B. On-Demand Instances.
  • C. Reserved Instances or a Savings Plan.
  • D. Dedicated Instances without a commitment.
Show Answer and Explanation

Correct answer: C. Stable, always-on usage with a known commitment suits a Reserved Instance or a Savings Plan, both of which give a discount for a one-year or three-year commitment.

OptionResultReason
AIncorrectSpot Instances can be interrupted, so they do not suit an always-available payroll application.
BIncorrectOn-Demand has no commitment and usually the highest price for steady usage.
CCorrectA one-year or three-year commitment gives a discount for predictable, continuous usage.
DIncorrectDedicated Instances address isolation. They are not the lowest-cost option for steady usage.

6. Knowledge Check

Answer each question in your own words before you open the model answer. The questions were written for this course.

Question 1: Name the three kinds of information that an AMI contains, and explain what you must do to launch an instance from your AMI in a different Region.

Maps to: Objective 1 (Knowledge and Comprehension).

An AMI contains a template for the root volume, launch permissions, and a block device mapping. An AMI belongs to one Region, so you copy it to the other Region, with the EC2 console, the AWS CLI, or the CopyImage API action, and then launch the instance from the copy, which has a new AMI ID.

Question 2: Decode the instance type c7gn.xlarge. What does each part of the name represent?

Maps to: Objective 2 (Comprehension).

The c is the instance family, compute optimized. The 7 is the generation, the seventh. The letters gn are the processor and capabilities: g means AWS Graviton processors, and n means network and EBS optimized. The xlarge is the size within the family.

Question 3: Name three EC2 instance states in which AWS does not bill for compute.

Maps to: Objective 1 (Knowledge).

The pending, stopped, shutting-down, and terminated states are not billed, and the stopping state is not billed when the instance is preparing to stop. The running state is billed, and the stopping state is billed when the instance is preparing to hibernate.

Question 4: Give the default port for SSH access to Linux instances, for RDP access to Windows instances, and for HTTPS traffic.

Maps to: Objective 3 (Knowledge).

SSH uses port 22, RDP uses port 3389, and HTTPS uses port 443.

Question 5: When you connect by SSH, which key is stored on your local computer, and which is stored on the EC2 instance?

Maps to: Objective 6 (Comprehension).

The private key is stored on your local computer, and the public key is stored on the EC2 instance. You get only one chance to download the private key, so store it securely.

Question 6: Which service provides persistent, network-attached block storage for EC2, and what is the temporary storage that is erased when you stop or terminate an instance?

Maps to: Objective 1 (Knowledge).

Amazon EBS provides persistent network-attached block storage. The EC2 instance store provides temporary storage that AWS deletes when you stop, hibernate, or terminate the instance.

Question 7: A video transcoding pipeline runs continuous, heavy CPU calculations. A low-traffic staging environment needs only occasional CPU bursts. Which instance family fits each?

Maps to: Objective 5 (Application).

Use a compute optimized family (C) for the transcoding pipeline, because the work is CPU-bound. Use a burstable general purpose family (T) for the staging environment, because it stays low-cost when idle and can burst during tests.

Question 8: Explain how a security group controls traffic to an instance, and how you would block one specific IP address.

Maps to: Objective 6 (Analysis).

A security group is a stateful virtual firewall with allow rules only. Inbound traffic is denied unless a rule allows it, and response traffic is allowed automatically. Because it has no deny rules, you block one IP address with a network access control list at the subnet level.

Question 9: Match a workload to a pricing model: a two-week test, a continuously running payroll application for three years, a restartable batch job, and software licensed per physical socket.

Maps to: Objective 4 (Application).

Use On-Demand Instances for the two-week test, a Reserved Instance or a Savings Plan for the steady payroll application, Spot Instances for the restartable batch job, and Dedicated Hosts for the socket-licensed software.
